scene: One plain round plate on a plain table seen from slightly above, a fork beside it. The plate is smooth and empty, with three small sparkle marks near its rim and a folded cloth lying next to it. No stains, crumbs or marks anywhere on the plate.
must: a smooth empty plate with sparkle marks and a cloth.
avoid: a plate with a few crumbs (vuil); a plate with one small spot (vuil); a bare plate with no sparkles and no cloth (leeg); a shiny new plate in its box (nieuw).
contrast: Pair with vuil. The only difference is the surface of the plate: spotless with sparkles here, smeared with stains and crumbs there.
example_nl: Na het wassen zijn mijn handen schoon.
example_en: After washing my hands are clean.
alt: Een leeg bord met een vork ernaast; langs de rand staan drie kleine sterretjes.

scene: One plain round plate on a plain table seen from slightly above, a fork beside it. The plate is smeared with several large irregular stains and scattered crumbs, and a few small flies hover above it. The fork also carries a smear.
must: a plate covered in stains, crumbs and flies.
avoid: a clean plate with sparkles (schoon); a plate with food on it (not the card); a broken plate (kapot); a wet plate with water drops (nat).
contrast: Pair with schoon. The only difference is the surface of the plate: stains, crumbs and flies here, a spotless plate with sparkles there.
example_nl: De sokken zijn erg vuil.
example_en: The socks are very dirty.
alt: Op een bord liggen grote vlekken en kruimels, en er vliegen kleine vliegjes boven.

scene: One plain shirt hanging by two pegs from a straight washing line, front view, bare plain wall behind. Heavy drops fall from the hem into a wide puddle on the ground below. Nothing falls from the sky: no rain strokes and no clouds.
must: drops falling from the shirt into a puddle.
avoid: the same shirt with no drops and no puddle (droog); a rain cloud over the line (not the card); a bucket of water (not the card); a swimming pool (not the card).
contrast: Pair with droog. The only difference is the water: drops and a puddle here, none there.
example_nl: Mijn jas is nat van de regen.
example_en: My coat is wet from the rain.
alt: Een shirt hangt aan een lijn; onderaan druipen druppels in een plas.

scene: One plain shirt hanging by two pegs from a straight washing line, front view, bare plain wall behind, the cloth in the same folds. No drops fall from the hem, and the ground below is bare and clean with no puddle. No sun and no clouds in the picture.
must: a hanging shirt above bare ground with no drops.
avoid: the same shirt dripping into a puddle (nat); a sun shining on the line (not the card); an empty washing line (not the card); a desert with cracked ground (not the card).
contrast: Pair with nat. The only difference is the water: no drops and bare ground here, drops and a puddle there.
example_nl: Gelukkig is de handdoek weer droog.
example_en: Luckily the towel is dry again.
alt: Een shirt hangt aan een lijn; de grond eronder is kaal en schoon.

scene: One plain book standing upright on a plain shelf board, with a pencil leaning beside it for scale. The book is very thick: its spine is as wide as the whole pencil is long, and many page edges are drawn along its side. The cover is blank, with no title or writing.
must: an upright book with a spine as wide as a pencil is long.
avoid: a thin book (dun); a tall narrow book (hoog); a wide flat book lying down (breed); a pile of three thin books (not the card).
contrast: Pair with dun. The only difference is the thickness of the book: a spine as wide as the pencil's length here, a spine as wide as the pencil's tip there.
example_nl: Ik lees een dik boek.
example_en: I am reading a thick book.
alt: Een boek staat rechtop naast een potlood; de rug is net zo breed als het potlood lang is.

scene: One plain book standing upright on a plain shelf board, with a pencil leaning beside it for scale. The book is very thin: its spine is no wider than the pencil's tip, and only two or three page edges are drawn along its side. The cover is blank, with no title or writing.
must: an upright book with a spine no wider than a pencil tip.
avoid: a thick book (dik); a short small book (klein); a book lying flat (not the card); a single sheet of paper (not the card).
contrast: Pair with dik. The only difference is the thickness of the book: a spine as wide as the pencil's tip here, a spine as wide as the pencil's length there.
example_nl: Het papier is te dun.
example_en: The paper is too thin.
alt: Een boek staat rechtop naast een potlood; de rug is niet breder dan de punt van het potlood.

scene: One adult standing in the middle of a straight plain path seen from the front, arms hanging. The path edges, with grass beyond, lie far from the shoulders on both sides, and the path is wide enough for three more people to stand beside the adult.
must: path edges far from the person's shoulders on both sides.
avoid: a narrow path with the edges at the shoulders (smal); a long road going to the horizon (lang); a tall person (groot); a field with no path (not the card).
contrast: Pair with smal. The only difference is the width of the path: edges far from the shoulders here, edges at the shoulders there.
example_nl: De straat is breed genoeg voor bussen.
example_en: The street is wide enough for buses.
alt: Een man staat midden op een pad; de randen liggen aan beide kanten ver van zijn schouders.

scene: One adult standing in the middle of a straight plain path seen from the front, arms hanging. The grass edges of the path run right at the shoulders on both sides, so there is no room for a second person beside the adult.
must: path edges at the person's shoulders, arms hanging.
avoid: a wide path with room for many people (breed); a thin person (dun); a short path (kort); a path ending in a fence (not the card).
contrast: Pair with breed. The only difference is the width of the path: edges at the shoulders here, edges far from the shoulders there.
example_nl: Het pad in het bos is smal.
example_en: The path in the forest is narrow.
alt: Een man staat midden op een pad; het gras raakt aan beide kanten zijn schouders.

scene: One plain room seen from the front with its window, table, chair and one table lamp. The curtains are closed, the lamp is switched off and drawn without rays, and one adult in the middle shuffles forward with both hands stretched out in front, feeling the way, eyes wide.
must: closed curtains, an unlit lamp and a person feeling the way with outstretched hands.
avoid: the same room with open curtains and a lamp with rays (licht-kamer); a night sky with moon and stars (not the card); a person sleeping in bed (not the card); a blindfolded person (not the card).
contrast: Pair with licht-kamer. The only difference is the light: curtains closed, the lamp off and the person groping here, curtains open, rays and the person walking normally there.
example_nl: Het is donker in de kelder.
example_en: It is dark in the cellar.
alt: Een man loopt met uitgestoken handen door een kamer; de gordijnen zijn dicht en de lamp is uit.

scene: One plain room seen from the front with its window, table, chair and one table lamp. The curtains are pulled open, bold sun rays stream through the window across the floor, the lamp has short rays around it, and one adult walks through the middle normally, arms swinging.
must: open curtains with rays through the window and a lamp with rays.
avoid: the same room with closed curtains and a groping person (donker); a box held up in one hand (licht-gewicht); a window with the sun outside only (not the card); a lamp shown on its own (not the card).
contrast: Pair with donker. The only difference is the light: curtains open, rays and the person walking normally here, curtains closed, the lamp off and the person groping there.
example_nl: De kamer is lekker licht.
example_en: The room is nice and light.
alt: Een man loopt door een kamer; de gordijnen zijn open en brede stralen vallen door het raam en om de lamp.

scene: One plain kitchen knife lying flat on a wooden board next to one small round apple. The blade tapers to a hair-thin edge, and the apple beside it has already been cut cleanly into two halves. Nothing else is on the board.
must: a knife with a hair-thin edge beside an apple cut in two.
avoid: a knife with a rounded thick edge (bot); a pointed spike (not the card); a pair of scissors (not the card); a long thin blade (dun).
contrast: Pair with bot. The only difference is the edge of the blade: a hair-thin edge and a cut apple here, a thick rounded edge and a whole apple there.
example_nl: Pas op, het mes is scherp.
example_en: Be careful, the knife is sharp.
alt: Een mes ligt op een plank met een dunne snijkant; de appel ernaast is doormidden.

scene: One plain kitchen knife lying flat on a wooden board next to one small round apple. The blade ends in a thick rounded edge, and the apple beside it is whole, with only a small dent where the knife pressed. Nothing else is on the board.
must: a knife with a thick rounded edge beside an uncut apple.
avoid: a knife with a hair-thin edge (scherp); a broken knife (kapot); a thick heavy blade (dik); a spoon (not the card).
contrast: Pair with scherp. The only difference is the edge of the blade: a thick rounded edge and a whole apple here, a hair-thin edge and a cut apple there.
example_nl: Mijn schaar is te bot.
example_en: My scissors are too blunt.
alt: Een mes ligt op een plank met een dikke ronde rand; de appel ernaast is nog in één stuk.

scene: One plain cup with a handle standing on a plain table, side view. The cup is in one piece: the rim is a smooth unbroken oval, the handle is attached, and no lines run across the body. Nothing else is on the table.
must: a cup with an unbroken rim and its handle attached.
avoid: a cup in pieces (kapot); a cup with one crack line (kapot); a full cup of tea (vol); a new cup in its packing box (nieuw).
contrast: Pair with kapot. The only difference is the state of the cup: one smooth piece with its handle here, separate pieces and a loose handle there.
example_nl: Gelukkig is de vaas nog heel.
example_en: Luckily the vase is still whole.
alt: Een kopje met oor staat op tafel; de rand is een gladde ononderbroken lijn.

scene: One plain cup standing on a plain table, side view, broken into three large pieces with small gaps between them and a few tiny splinters beside. The handle lies detached on the table. Nothing else is on the table.
must: a cup split into pieces with the handle lying loose.
avoid: a whole cup with its handle (heel); a cup tipped over with a spill (not the card); a cup with a chipped rim (not the card); a dirty cup with stains (vuil).
contrast: Pair with heel. The only difference is the state of the cup: separate pieces and a loose handle here, one smooth piece with its handle there.
example_nl: De telefoon van mijn vader is kapot.
example_en: My father's phone is broken.
alt: Een kopje ligt in drie stukken op tafel; het oor ligt los ernaast.

scene: One adult man sitting at a plain table, upper body, front view, an empty plate with a fork laid across it in front of him. His hands are folded on the table, the brows are relaxed, the eyes calm and open, and the mouth shows a gentle smile.
must: an empty plate, folded hands and a gentle smile.
avoid: a full plate pushed away with one mouth corner down (ontevreden); a hand on a round stomach (vol); a wide laughing face with an open mouth (blij); a sleeping face (not the card).
contrast: Pair with ontevreden. The only difference is the plate and the face: an empty plate, folded hands and a gentle smile here, a full plate pushed away and one mouth corner down there.
example_nl: Ik ben tevreden met mijn nieuwe fiets.
example_en: I am satisfied with my new bike.
alt: Een man zit aan tafel achter een leeg bord, vouwt zijn handen en glimlacht zacht.

scene: One adult man sitting at a plain table, upper body, front view, pushing a full plate of food away from him toward the far edge with one hand. The brows are level, not pulled into a V, the eyes look away from the plate, and one corner of the mouth turns down.
must: a full plate pushed away and one corner of the mouth down.
avoid: an empty plate, folded hands and a smile (tevreden); V-shaped brows and a tight mouth (boos); a face with tears (verdrietig); a full plate and a hand on the stomach (vol).
contrast: Pair with tevreden. The only difference is the plate and the face: a full plate pushed away and one mouth corner down here, an empty plate, folded hands and a gentle smile there.
example_nl: De klant is ontevreden over het eten.
example_en: The customer is dissatisfied with the food.
alt: Een man duwt een bord met eten van zich af; één mondhoek hangt naar beneden.

scene: One plain table with four chairs and cups, seen from the front, with one window behind. A single small adult sits at one end with one cup in front, shoulders down and a sad face with a drooping mouth, looking at the three empty chairs. The rest of the table is bare.
must: one person with a sad face at a table of empty chairs.
avoid: four people sitting close and talking (gezellig); a person reading happily alone (alleen); a person asleep at a table (not the card); a person waiting at a bus stop (not the card).
contrast: Pair with gezellig. The only difference is the company: one person and empty chairs here, four people sitting close together there.
example_nl: Hij woont alleen en voelt zich eenzaam.
example_en: He lives alone and feels lonely.
alt: Een man zit alleen aan een tafel met een kopje en kijkt naar drie lege stoelen.

scene: One plain table with chairs and cups, seen from the front, with one window behind. Four adults sit close together around it, every chair taken, leaning towards each other, smiling and talking with their hands, and each has a cup in front.
must: four people sitting close around a table, smiling and talking.
avoid: one person alone at a table with empty chairs (eenzaam); a noisy crowded party (not the card); people sitting apart and not talking (eenzaam); people arguing with frowns (not the card).
contrast: Pair with eenzaam. The only difference is the company: four people close together and talking here, one person and empty chairs there.
example_nl: Het is gezellig bij mijn oma.
example_en: It is cosy at my grandma's.
alt: Vier mensen zitten dicht bij elkaar aan een tafel, lachen en praten met kopjes voor zich.

scene: One adult standing, front view, upper body and both arms visible. The shoulders are pulled up towards the ears, both hands are clenched into fists, neck lines show on the throat, the jaw is set and the brows are drawn together.
must: raised shoulders and clenched fists with neck lines showing.
avoid: a person with open hands and low shoulders (ontspannen); a person wringing the hands and tapping a foot (zenuwachtig); a person leaning away from a threat (bang); a person shouting with V-shaped brows (boos); a person lifting a heavy box (zwaar).
contrast: Pair with ontspannen. The only difference is the body: raised shoulders, fists and neck lines here, low shoulders, open hands and a soft face there.
example_nl: De spelers zijn gespannen voor de wedstrijd.
example_en: The players are tense before the match.
alt: Een man staat met opgetrokken schouders en gebalde vuisten; op zijn nek staan streepjes.

scene: One adult standing, front view, upper body and both arms visible. The shoulders hang low and level, both arms dangle loosely with open hands, the neck is smooth, the jaw is soft and the mouth shows a slight easy smile.
must: low shoulders, loose open hands and a soft smile.
avoid: a person with raised shoulders and fists (gespannen); a person sitting back in a waiting-room chair (kalm); a person lying asleep (not the card); a person slouching with a sad face (verdrietig).
contrast: Pair with gespannen. The only difference is the body: low shoulders, open hands and a soft face here, raised shoulders, fists and neck lines there.
example_nl: Op zondag ben ik lekker ontspannen.
example_en: On Sunday I am nicely relaxed.
alt: Een man staat met lage schouders en losse armen; zijn handen zijn open en hij glimlacht licht.

scene: One plain pillow lying on a plain bed, side view, with a small cup beside it for scale. The pillow has sunk completely: its top is a straight level line no higher than the cup's handle, and the cloth lies in a few shallow wrinkles.
must: a pillow whose top is a straight low line.
avoid: a puffed pillow with a domed top (bol); a thin sheet of paper (dun); a level road across the page (vlak); a pillow standing on its edge (not the card).
contrast: Pair with bol. The only difference is the top of the pillow: a straight low line here, a high rounded dome there.
example_nl: Mijn kussen is helemaal plat.
example_en: My pillow is completely flat.
alt: Een kussen ligt op een bed; de bovenkant is een rechte, lage lijn naast een klein kopje.

scene: One plain pillow lying on a plain bed, side view, with a small cup beside it for scale. The pillow is plump: its top rises in a smooth high dome, about twice as high as the cup, with the sides bulging outward.
must: a pillow with a smooth high dome on top.
avoid: a flat pillow with a straight top (plat); a round ball (not the card); a pointed hill (not the card); a thick book (dik).
contrast: Pair with plat. The only difference is the top of the pillow: a high rounded dome here, a straight low line there.
example_nl: De wangen van de baby zijn bol.
example_en: The baby's cheeks are round and plump.
alt: Een kussen ligt op een bed; de bovenkant rijst als een ronde heuvel boven een klein kopje.

scene: one small tree and one washing line with three towels in a plain garden, front view, a plain fence behind, a plain sky. The tree bends hard to the right, three leaves fly off through the air, and the towels stand out sideways from the line, flapping, with four long wavy air lines crossing the picture.
must: the tree bent over and the towels standing out sideways.
avoid: a still tree and towels hanging straight down (windstil); rain falling (nat); a whirlwind lifting a roof (gevaarlijk); a man shivering (koud).
contrast: Pair with windstil. The only difference is the air: a bent tree and towels flying sideways here, a still tree and towels hanging straight down there.
example_nl: Aan zee is het vaak winderig.
example_en: By the sea it is often windy.
alt: Een boompje buigt ver opzij en de handdoeken aan de waslijn waaien opzij.

scene: the same small tree and washing line with three towels in a plain garden, front view, a plain fence behind, a plain sky. The tree stands perfectly upright with every leaf hanging still, and the three towels hang straight down from the line without a fold moving. No lines in the air.
must: an upright tree and towels hanging straight down.
avoid: a bent tree and towels flying sideways (winderig); a sun with long rays (zonnig); stiff dry towels (droog); an empty washing line (leeg).
contrast: Pair with winderig. The only difference is the air: a still tree and towels hanging straight down here, a bent tree and towels flying sideways there.
example_nl: Het is windstil, dus de zee is vlak.
example_en: There is no wind, so the sea is flat.
alt: Een boompje staat recht en de handdoeken hangen roerloos aan de waslijn.
